evidence.claim: A minimum-boiling ternary azeotrope of 83.1 % ethyl acetate, 8.7 % ethanol and 8.2 % water (mass) prevents taking pure ethyl acetate by simple distillation.
limits: The composition is cited by the authors from their ref. 22; pressure not stated in this passage.

evidence.claim: The first column needs an azeotropic agent because the reaction releases more water (about 17 %) than the azeotrope carries (about 7.8 %); the recycled organic phase of the extraction (>93 % ester) is that agent.

quantities.name: water released by the reaction
quantities.basis: authors' approximate figure, basis not stated

quantities.name: ester in the recycled organic phase

limits: Approximate figures cited by the authors (refs 8, 29).

evidence.claim: Esterification runs in a reactor-evaporator at about 90 C and atmospheric pressure; its vapour feeds the azeotropic column, whose acid-rich bottoms return to the reactor.
limits: The paper's Table 1 gives 85-90 C.

evidence.claim: UNIQUAC is used for both vapour-liquid and liquid-liquid equilibria, chosen from the fits reported by Calvar (VLE) and Arce (LLE).
limits: Parameters not printed.

evidence.claim: The azeotrope may hold at most 0.005 wt% acetic acid; the authors meet it with R/V above 0.5 and at least 14 theoretical stages.
limits: Table 1 of the same paper gives column 5 only 8 stages and R/V 0.61 (a discrepancy kept by the case).

evidence.claim: Cooling the azeotrope before extraction is limited by cooling water to 20-30 C; the optimum water-to-azeotrope mass ratio is 1 to 2 (more water enriches the organic phase but loses ester and makes more wastewater).

quantities.name: water to azeotrope mass ratio, lower end
water to azeotrope mass ratio, upper end

limits: Modelled by the authors in Chemcad 7, not measured.

evidence.claim: The product column must give at least 99.9 wt% ester with water below 0.03 wt% and ethanol below 0.04 wt%; 99.9 % from R/D 1.5, both impurity limits from R/D 2.25, optimum R/D 3-3.5.
limits: At a fixed product rate (Section 3.4); the paper's own Table A2 leaves 0.07 % water at R/D 3.

evidence.claim: The wastewater column's bottoms must contain less than 0.01 wt% organics.
limits: An assumption of the authors' design.

evidence.claim: S2 settings: column 5 8 stages, feed stage 8, R/V 0.61; column 11 35 stages, feed 15, R/D 3; column 15 18 stages, feed 9, R/D 2; reactor-evaporator 85-90 C, 300 m3, 13,586.2 kW; extractor 70 C, W/A 1.
limits: Text layer of a table; column positions read by an AI session.

evidence.claim: S2 Table A2: feed 13 (27,314 kg/h, 4.70 % water, 0.01 % acid), distillate 14 (230.4 kmol/h, 8.57 % water) and product 16 (141.5 kmol/h, 12,434 kg/h, 99.90 % ester, 0.07 % water, 0.02 % ethanol, 0.01 % acid).
limits: Lab's reading (case README): the paper's product water 0.07 % exceeds its own 0.03 % limit, and all of feed 13's acid must leave in the product (0.022 %, not 0.01 %).

evidence.claim: S2 Table A2: wash-water recycle 23 is 95,797 kg/h and wastewater 25 is 20,000 kg/h (a round number, as in S1 and S3, while fresh water 17 is not).
limits: Whether 20,000 kg/h is a specification is Lab's inference (not stated in the paper).

decisions.expected_change: Ethyl acetate as the bottoms, meeting the paper's product purity.
limits: CHEPTA 0.6.2 returns NO_CONVERGENCE at all three flows; this says nothing about the paper's own simulator.

keys.statement: The paper's literature review names extractive distillation with a heavy solvent, and pervaporation, for this azeotrope, and rejects both because each needs a second method to reach product purity.

decisions.obstacle: The ester-alcohol-water azeotrope blocks ordinary distillation.
decisions.mechanism: A heavy solvent changes the relative volatility (extractive distillation).
decisions.operation: Extractive distillation with a heavy solvent, named in the paper's review without results of its own.
decisions.expected_change: Break the azeotrope; per the review, not to product purity without a second method.

decisions.obstacle: Esterification of ethanol with acetic acid is reversible and nearly thermoneutral, so conversion is limited by equilibrium.
decisions.mechanism: Products leave as vapour as they form, shifting the equilibrium; unreacted acid returns from the azeotropic column's bottoms.
decisions.operation: Reactor-evaporator at 85-90 C and atmospheric pressure, 300 m3 (Table 1), vapour to column 5, column 5 bottoms back to the reactor.
decisions.expected_change: High overall acid conversion with the acid recycled until used up.
limits: The paper's own simulated design (Chemcad 7); its rate law could not be reused by Lab (catalyst concentration and units missing; case README).
Draft, written by an AI session from the case files (2026-11-20); not reviewed.

decisions.obstacle: Unreacted acetic acid in the reactor vapour must stay out of the ester azeotrope (at most 0.005 wt%).
decisions.mechanism: A column without condenser or reboiler washes the reactor vapour with the recycled ester-rich organic phase as reflux; acid goes down and back to the reactor.
decisions.operation: Column 5: reactor vapour on the last stage, organic phase of the extractor (60,000 kg/h) on stage 1; Table 1: 8 stages, R/V 0.61.
decisions.expected_change: Azeotrope overhead with acid below 0.005 wt%; acid-rich bottoms to the reactor.
limits: Section 3.2 asks for at least 14 stages while Table 1 gives 8; the paper's own stream 8 prints 0.01 % acid against the 0.005 % limit (case README, discrepancies).
Draft, written by an AI session from the case files (2026-11-20); not reviewed.

decisions.obstacle: The reaction releases more water than the azeotrope can carry overhead, so water would accumulate in the reactor.
decisions.mechanism: The extractor's organic phase, richer in ester than the azeotrope, is fed back as reflux and binds the excess water into the azeotrope.
decisions.operation: Part of the organic phase (stream 26) returned to column 5 as reflux; the rest goes to the product column.
decisions.expected_change: All reaction water leaves overhead as azeotrope, none accumulates in the reactor.
limits: Author-stated reason with approximate figures (17 % and 7.8 % water).
Draft, written by an AI session from the case files (2026-11-20); not reviewed.

decisions.obstacle: More wash water enriches the organic phase in ester but loses ester to the water and makes more wastewater to distil.
decisions.mechanism: A trade-off between the organic phase's purity and the ester loss and wastewater load.
decisions.operation: Water-to-azeotrope mass ratio 1 in S2 (Table 1); the paper's sensitivity gives 1 to 2 as the optimum.
decisions.expected_change: Enough ethanol removed from the organic phase without excessive ester loss.
limits: Modelled by the authors, not measured.
Draft, written by an AI session from the case files (2026-11-20); not reviewed.

decisions.obstacle: The wash water leaves the extractor with ethanol and ester that must be recovered, and the wastewater must be nearly free of organics.
decisions.mechanism: Distil the organics overhead and return them to the reactor; water leaves at the bottom.
decisions.operation: Column 15: 18 stages, feed 9, R/D 2 (Table 1); distillate 21 back to the reactor; bottoms split into wash-water recycle and wastewater.
decisions.expected_change: Wastewater bottoms below 0.01 wt% organics; ethanol and ester recovered.
limits: The paper's own stream 22 prints 0.03 % organics, and the feed's 0.01 % acid alone leaves about 0.012 % in the bottoms (case README, round 2).
Draft, written by an AI session from the case files (2026-11-20); not reviewed.

decisions.obstacle: The wash water circulates; water formed by the reaction and the make-up must leave somewhere.
decisions.mechanism: Recycle most of the wastewater column's bottoms as wash water, purge the rest, add fresh water.
decisions.operation: Wastewater 25 = 20,000 kg/h, recycle 23 = 95,797 kg/h, fresh water 17 = 17,478 kg/h (Table A2).
decisions.expected_change: A closed wash-water loop with one wastewater exit.
limits: That 20,000 kg/h is the authors' specification is Lab's inference from the round numbers in S1-S3 (case README, round 2); the paper does not say so.
Draft, written by an AI session from the case files (2026-11-20); not reviewed.

decisions.obstacle: The paper's rate law cannot be used (catalyst concentration and concentration units missing) and CHEPTA has no kinetic reactor-evaporator.
decisions.mechanism: CHEPTA's conversion reactor with an all-vapour outlet (VF 1) is the reactor-evaporator; the acid conversion per pass is taken from the paper's streams 5 and 6.
decisions.operation: Conversion of acetic acid per pass 0.7703 = 1 - 4.74/20.64 (Table A2 streams 5 and 6), saturated-vapour outlet, the paper's inlet stream 5.
decisions.expected_change: The paper's reactor outlet and duty, without predicting the reaction.
limits: Outlet 89.0 C vs 90 C, duty 14,437 vs 13,586.2 kW (+6.3 %; case README, units table). The reactor is not predicted: conversion is imposed.
An equilibrium reactor at 90 C (run u-krea4-equilibrium-90C) is a different unit; it leaves 3.21 % acid in the vapour against the paper's 4.74 %.
